card.text: Ultracool red dwarf in Aquarius with seven Earth-sized planets.

introduction.text: TRAPPIST-1 is a star the size of Jupiter, 12.5 parsecs away. Seven transiting planets orbit it, all of them closer than Mercury is to the Sun.

color.title: Photosphere color
color.summary: The color of the star's light, dimmed and reddened toward the edge by a model atmosphere; no resolved image.

sources.label: Claret et al. 2012
sources.locator: tableab.dat, quadratic law by least squares: the R, V and B rows at 2,500 and 2,600 K, log g 5.0 and 5.5

habitable-zone.title: Conservative and optimistic zones
habitable-zone.summary: Where a planet with enough air could keep liquid water, as calculated. Darker: conservative limits; lighter: optimistic.

sources.label: Habitable Zone Gallery
sources.locator: Rows of TRAPPIST-1: its star's four habitable zone distances in au

stellar-wind.title: Wind pressure and magnetic boundary
stellar-wind.summary: A model of the star's wind: yellow where it presses hardest. Inside the dashed line its magnetic field still holds the wind.

sources.label: Garraffo et al. (2017)
sources.locator: Figure 3, left: the wind's total pressure in the plane of the orbits and the Alfvén surface, for a 600 G field

tidal-heating.title: Heat from tides, planet by planet
tidal-heating.summary: Each orbit in the color of the heat tides raise in its planet: most in b and c, little in d to f, none in g and h.

sources.label: Barr, Dobos & Kiss (2018)
sources.locator: Table 3: tidal heat flux of each planet in W/m²

brightness-campaign-12.title: Brightness map, Campaign 12
brightness-campaign-12.summary: Darker and brighter longitudes of the star, worked out in this project from how its light changes as it turns.

color-brightness.title: Color + brightness, Dec 2016 to Mar 2017
color-brightness.summary: The star in its own color, darker where its light shows it darker; the contrast is drawn stronger to be seen.
